entities.summary: Bodhidharma (b. 483 CE, Kanchipuram) was a philosopher or thinker of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Kanchipuram. He is known for founding Chan Buddhism, a school of Mahayana Buddhism that emphasized individual enlightenment and the attainment of Nirvana through meditation and physical discipline. His teachings and legacy have had a profound impact on East Asian spirituality and culture, shaping the development of Zen Buddhism and influencing Chinese and Japanese thought. Bodhidharma's significance extends beyond his own lifetime, as his ideas have been transmitted and reinterpreted over the centuries, influencing art, literature, and philosophy in China, Japan, and Korea. The exact dates of his life are unknown, but it is believed that he died in 543 CE, during the Northern Wei dynasty in China.
